- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00–0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion or hidden support.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 1–3% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply a lagged correction: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day of sentiment decay.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates in early periods (days 1–7) when sentiment is positive; apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias to first 7 days.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.67–0.00), model exhibits erratic behavior; use a smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day average) to reduce noise in forecast adjustments.
